item.title: Tourist hot spot faces housing revolt as locals demand cuts to vacation lodging
item.description: Mallorca, Spain, welcomed 13.5 million visitors in 2025, and now a business leader says the popular island must curb tourism and cut vacation rental capacity.
item.content:encoded:
One of Spain's most popular vacation islands is facing calls for a limit on tourist accommodations in order to curb crowding.

Jordi Mora, president of Pimem, a federation representing small and medium-sized businesses in Mallorca, said the island needs to take stronger steps to control tourism, according to the Majorca Daily Bulletin.

"We need to curb tourism, which includes reducing the total number of tourist beds," Mora told the outlet.

POPULAR DESTINATION CRACKS DOWN HARD ON TOURISTS AS NEW LIMITS THREATEN SUMMER GETAWAYS

Mallorca, one of the Balearic Islands, received some 13.5 million visitors in 2025, a significant number for an island measuring roughly 1,400 square miles, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Mora's proposal would include reducing the number of accommodations available in registered vacation rentals and taking stronger action against illegal rentals, the Majorca Daily Bulletin reported. Fox News Digital reached out to Pimem for comment.

Mora said some smaller hotel operators would support reducing accommodations if the changes were made through agreements and incentives.

"If this is approached through consensus and incentives, it is possible to move toward a more sustainable model," Mora said.

A travel expert previously discussed the issues faced by the Balearic Island with Fox News Digital.

"Once a place goes viral, it can get flooded with visitors really quickly. It’s great that people want to explore new places, but those places aren’t always set up to handle that kind of attention," travel expert Jordi Lippe-McGraw said. 

"That’s when you start to see overcrowding, higher costs for locals and more pressure on the area overall."

Mallorca has also been exploring a shift toward attracting fewer visitors who spend more money.

Pedro Homar, managing director of Palma's tourism board, said Mallorca would prefer to attract wealthy American tourists, Fox News Digital reported.

"Tourism is our way of life," Homar told The Wall Street Journal. "The change of model is quality over quantity. We need to have fewer tourists who spend more."

American tourists in Spain spent about $410 per day this past July, compared with $240 for German visitors and $260 for British travelers, according to The Wall Street Journal.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Mora also said the island does not need more tourists to grow its economy.

"We must increase value and ensure that this growth benefits society as a whole," he told the Majorca Daily Bulletin.

The clash with residents is especially noticeable in Mallorca, where thousands took to the streets in June 2025 to protest the growth of tourism on the island, Fox News Digital reported at the time.

Demonstrators marched with signs saying, "One more tourist, one less resident."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Mallorca's large visitor numbers have also brought other tourism concerns into focus.

Viral videos over the summer appeared to show pickpockets targeting tourists near Palma, including older visitors near popular attractions, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Travel expert Angel Castellanos told Fox News Digital at the time that crowded tourist areas can create opportunities for thieves, particularly when visitors are distracted or unfamiliar with their surroundings.

"The takeaway isn't to avoid these places," Castellanos said. "It's to travel smarter."

Andrea Margolis of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: MLW's Trevor Lee set for major high-stakes match against Yota Tsuji at Saturday Night SuperFight
item.description: Trevor Lee called out IWGP heavyweight champion Yota Tsuji for a massive showdown at MLW's Saturday Night SuperFight in Chicago this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Trevor Lee officially signed with Major League Wrestling (MLW) seven months ago and he has kept his foot on the gas pedal since stepping in between the ropes for the company.

Lee has gone toe-to-toe with some of the best MLW has to offer, including Kushida, Austin Aries and Místico, while also holding the MLW Southern Crown Championship. He broke the news with OutKick Dropkick/Fox News Digital in April and said at the time he had been waiting for a good opportunity to come his way.

Now, he’s making the most of it.

Lee will have a chance to make a statement at Saturday Night SuperFight this weekend when he steps into the ring with IWGP heavyweight champion Yota Tsuji, who is a superstar with New Japan Pro-Wrestling.

"I think it’s been going great," Lee told OutKick Dropkick of his time with MLW so far. "I think with the last time we spoke, I probably said something along the lines of, I just want to go out there and show what I can do, and I feel like over these past few months, I've had the capability to do that. I think that we're gonna be looking at even more opportunity coming this Saturday when I wrestle Yota. I mean, I couldn't ask for a better opportunity, right? The IWGP heavyweight champion. I'm looking at this match like kind of like a job interview, right? And, what a way to, what a way to try to start it out."

Lee was the one who called out Tsuji for this match at one of MLW’s biggest shows of the year.

MLW'S COURT BAUER TOUTS 'HUGE YEAR' FOR COMPANY AMID MEDIA DEALS, SPLASH MOVES

Tsuji is a two-time IWGP heavyweight champion, two-time IWGP global heavyweight champion and has held the IWGP Intercontinental Championship and the NEVER Openweight 6-Man Tag Team Championship one-time each.

The stakes are as high as they could be going into this match.

"I wanna show that I'm ready for that opportunity and if we're gonna bring these guys in and we're gonna highlight these guys as being the top guys that they truly are, Yota is the top of the top at New Japan," he continued. "So, if he's gonna come over here and he's gonna ask for a fight, then, you know, I'm looking for an opportunity. And I told you that right the last time we spoke, that I'm just wanting opportunities and what bigger opportunity."

Tsuji already has a cast of wrestlers gunning for his title. Most recently, it was Boltin Oleg and Kenny Omega.

Though Saturday night’s match is a non-title fight, the potential of Lee pinning Tsuji may put him among the contenders for the IWGP Heavyweight Championship.

So, what better way to step in day one to show everybody, hey, I've already beat the top guy here and, and I'm ready to continue to do it again."

item.title: 'Wipe those tears from our eyes and play like 46': Lions defense turns Jack Campbell tragedy into fuel
item.description: Kelvin Sheppard reveals the emotional fourth-down blitz call he made for Jack Campbell and how "play like 46" became the Detroit Lions' rallying cry.
item.content:encoded:
The pain of watching Jack Campbell collapse helplessly on the Ford Field turf Sunday has not completely subsided for the Detroit Lions. It certainly is not forgotten by teammates on defense that spent those horrible moments wiping away tears as their captain lay motionless with a neck injury.

But four days later, following Campbell's mostly positive report about having lower body motion, the focus has shifted to how to continue handling the situation.

The prayers persist. That hasn't stopped.

LIONS' JACK CAMPBELL OPENS UP ABOUT NECK INJURY, ANNOUNCES LOWER BODY MOVEMENT BUT ACKNOWLEDGES CHALLENGES

But the anguish, despair and despondency are yielding to something different. Something better:

Inspiration.

"You're kidding yourself to say it's not hard for the players to see something like that happen to anyone, let alone a player of his stature, of his makeup, of his heart," Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said on Thursday. "And to think these players are going to walk back in here like nothing happened?

"So the theme has been, let's prepare and play like 46 – every day."

Sheppard said a key fourth-down calls he made toward the end of Sunday's game was calling a blitz against the Minnesota Vikings when that is not typical for the Lions. He said the message to players then was, "we're about to do this for 46," which is Campbell's number.

That approach has extended through this week.

"I wake up [thinking] 'what would 46 want me to do today?' Sheppard said. "Would he want us to sulk and feel sorry? I can guarantee you, y'all know Jack, absolutely not. He'd be p---ed off if he found out guys were crying and guys were about him. That's just his makeup.

"So that's what we're doing in everything we do. Every meeting I told the unit, every walkthrough, every play, you all know how Jack prepares. You all know how he plays. The way you honor him is to wipe those tears from your eyes and make sure we prepare and play like him.

"So that's the thing moving forward to this week."

This is good coaching.

Sheppard cannot deny the emotions his players invested on the scary and uncertain moments while Campbell was being placed on a immobilization board and carted off the field.

But the NFL season has not stopped since the game moved ahead. And like the game, the season continues for the Lions.

And so Sheppard is asking his defensive players to accept something horrible, acknowledge it, and not only overcome it but turn it into a tool.

"That is," Sheppard repeated "the theme for the week."

item.title: Bill Belichick advances once again as Pro Football Hall of Fame finalist after first-ballot snub in 2026
item.description: Bill Belichick advanced as one of five coaching finalists for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027 after his stunning first-ballot snub.
item.content:encoded:
Bill Belichick is back where he was last year, as he was among the five coaches that advanced in the process to potentially be elected into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

No one expected Belichick to still be on the ballot at this point, though, believing he deserved to be a first-ballot Hall of Famer. After all, he has the second-most wins by a head coach of all time, and some believe he is the greatest coach to ever grace an NFL sideline.

But, despite his many accolades and reverence in the sport, Belichick didn’t make the cut on his first ballot, sending the football world into massive debate and many of his former players speaking out in disgust. Belichick himself was "puzzled" and "disappointed" he wasn’t a first-ballot Hall of Famer, per ESPN.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

One year later, Belichick could, and should, be in the Hall of Fame Class of 2027, as the governing body announced that next step for him and four other coaches on Thursday.

Joining Belichick are great former coaches Tom Coughlin, Dan Reeves, Mike Holmgren and Mike Shanahan from the group of 14 who were considered. The coaching subcommittee will meet next on Nov. 17 to pick one from the final five to be presented in front of the voting committee for the 2027 class.

Belichick moved on in 2026, and it’s highly expected he will do so again. So, the question becomes: will he now get at least the 40 votes needed to be placed in Canton for eternity?

This is a head coach who tallied six Super Bowls with the New England Patriots, while owning two prior to that with the New York Giants as their defensive coordinator. There’s no question his resume speaks for itself, and he even told an associate, per ESPN, "Six Super Bowls isn’t enough?"

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After Belichick was snubbed, the Hall of Fame overhauled its selection process, cutting the voting committee down from 50 to 28, while ending formal presentations and merging the senior category with modern era.

The Hall says the changes are intended to "improve its selection process."

"The Hall continually reviews its bylaws to ensure the selection process reflects the highest standards of integrity and the magnitude of election to the Pro Football Hall of Fame," said Hall of Fame president Jim Porter in September. "There is no more important task at the Hall of Fame than the election of each new class."

Belichick is currently in his second season as the head coach of the North Carolina Tar Heels, who sit 4-4 on the year.

item.title: Sylvester Stallone says Hollywood abandoned Middle America as Taylor Sheridan found an ignored audience
item.description: Sylvester Stallone says Taylor Sheridan tapped into a Middle America audience Hollywood has ignored since John Wayne, and streaming is winning.
item.content:encoded:
Sylvester Stallone didn't hold back when it came to Hollywood's biggest blind spot.

The "Tulsa King" star explained Taylor Sheridan found success by giving a forgotten audience exactly what it had been missing. According to Stallone, Sheridan tapped into something Hollywood had long ignored: an audience eager for stories rooted in Middle America.

"It's very, very important because that audience was ignored for centuries, it seems, since John Wayne," Stallone explained during an appearance on "The Rest Is Entertainment." "And he really mined a consciousness like, 'Oh, we forgot about that guy in the middle of America.' They're always writing about California and New York."

TAYLOR SHERIDAN SAYS HOLLYWOOD DIDN’T BELIEVE IN 'YELLOWSTONE,' NOW IT’S A TV EMPIRE

"But the middle America, it's a different vibe," he added. "And so people were starving for it. It's like a simpler world and more, I would just say, confrontational."

Despite Sheridan's success, Stallone doesn't think Hollywood has caught up when it comes to film-making and what Middle America might be hoping to see on the big screen.

"But the beauty of streaming is they're fast, and they're nimble, and they can really put a show on the air in a matter of weeks," Stallone said.

Stallone's criticism of Hollywood comes as the industry prepares to revisit his own battle to get a story told on his terms.

Stallone's remarkable journey from struggling actor to Hollywood superstar is getting the big-screen treatment in "I Play Rocky," a 2026 biographical drama directed by Peter Farrelly.

The film follows Stallone's determination to write and star in the 1976 boxing classic, despite Hollywood executives initially resisting the idea of an unknown actor playing the lead.

Stallone didn't participate in the making of "I Play Rocky," explaining he felt the project would look like an "ego massaging vehicle" if he were involved.

"And then they showed me the fellow who was going to play me and I thought it was me," he said, referring to the film's star, Anthony Ippolito. "He gained weight. I mean, he looked the real deal."

Stallone became a household name because of the action film, which won the Academy Award for Best Picture. His five most recognizable films include "Rocky," "First Blood," "Rocky IV," "Cliffhanger," and "Creed." His portrayal of boxer Rocky Balboa and Vietnam veteran John Rambo helped establish him as one of Hollywood's most enduring action stars.

The actor found a new television audience with his starring role in "Tulsa King."

Stallone plays Dwight "The General" Manfredi, a New York Mafia capo who is released from prison after serving 25 years. Rather than being welcomed back into the criminal organization he protected, Dwight is sent to Tulsa, Oklahoma, where he begins building his own criminal empire with an unlikely group of associates.

item.title: Firefighter who battled COVID on front lines says he lost career for refusing vaccine: 'I'm on team Jesus'
item.description: Scott Carlson says he and fellow Redmond Fire Department firefighters were terminated after religious exemptions were revoked under a vaccine mandate.
item.content:encoded:
A veteran Washington state firefighter who helped respond to some of America's first COVID-19 patients says he lost the career he loved after refusing to violate his religious beliefs to comply with a vaccine mandate and is now fighting to have his day in court.

Scott Carlson, a former lieutenant with the Redmond Fire Department, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview that he and his colleagues spent 18 months on the front lines of the pandemic without a single case of cross-contamination before the city's vaccine requirements upended his career.

"We worked 18 months with zero cross-contaminations," Carlson said. "We did our job very well. And then the governor came out and said that they wanted us to get the COVID vaccine mandate."

WHO IS JAMES ERDMAN III? CIA WHISTLEBLOWER WHO WENT FROM COVID MANDATE FIGHTS TO SENATE SPOTLIGHT

But when Washington officials implemented COVID-19 vaccination requirements, Carlson said he sought a religious exemption in 2021, only to learn that he would not be permitted to continue working. First Liberty Institute, which is representing eight firefighters, did not elaborate on Carlson's behalf regarding his religious exemption request.

"I went through and applied for a religious exemption," Carlson recalled. "I had to prove that I was actually religious, and it wasn't just something I wanted.

"And then, about 10 days later, the mayor [Angela Birney] came back and got rid of all of that and said no, and then decided to terminate all of us."

According to court documents, Carlson filed a lawsuit against the City of Redmond in federal court Dec. 8, 2022, alleging that officials violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 by failing to accommodate his religious beliefs and retaliating against him for requesting an exemption from the COVID-19 vaccine mandate.

The lawsuit was later amended twice to include additional firefighters after they received notices from the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission granting them the right to sue, according to the court filing.

The firefighters are appealing a December 2025 federal district court ruling that sided with the City of Redmond, rejecting their claims that the city failed to accommodate their religious beliefs and retaliated against them for seeking exemptions from its COVID-19 vaccine mandate.

Their attorney, Cliff Martin, told Fox News Digital in an interview Wednesday that the case involves more than a disagreement over vaccine policy. He alleges the city had positions available that could have accommodated the firefighters but appeared to keep those opportunities from them.

OREGON SETTLES WITH CHRISTIAN MOTHER DENIED FOSTER CARE ADOPTION OVER GENDER IDENTITY BELIEFS

According to First Liberty, Carlson initially received religious exemptions before those accommodations were revoked after Redmond's mayor signed an executive order. The firefighters' attorneys allege that city officials subsequently withheld information about available positions that could have allowed the employees to remain on the job. 

The legal team is asking the 9th Circuit to overturn a lower court ruling that rejected their claims.

"We're at the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals, and we are hopeful that the circuit court will reverse a summary judgment order and will recognize and vindicate the victims of this religious discrimination," Martin told Fox News Digital.

Martin alleged that the employer could have transferred the firefighters into other roles where vaccination was not required.

"Instead, they hid those available positions from the plaintiffs and then filled them with vaccinated firefighters so that there was nowhere to transfer these unvaccinated firefighters who had a religious objection to the COVID vaccine," he said.

WASHINGTON SCHOOL DISTRICT THAT FORCED KIDS TO HIDE BIBLES IN SEALED ENVELOPES MUST APOLOGIZE, PAY $275K

Those allegations are central to the firefighters' legal challenge and have not been independently established in the interview material provided to Fox News Digital.

For Carlson, the consequences went far beyond losing a paycheck.

He said firefighting was a calling that allowed him to serve his community, use his skills and help others during some of the most difficult moments of their lives.

"The emotion of losing my career, and what I feel a little bit is what my purpose is, over my faith, that was a heart divided, because I love Jesus so much that I was like, ‘Hey, I'm going to follow you no matter what. I'm on team Jesus. But dang it, this is hard.’"

Carlson said the loss of his position meant losing an important part of how he served others.

"This is how I serve. This is how I love on the community," he said. "So, that was a very hard emotion to say that I'm no longer going to be able to do this."

Although the COVID-19 pandemic has faded from daily headlines, Carlson said the legal and personal consequences remain unresolved for people who lost their jobs during the vaccine mandate era.

TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS

"A lot of people say, ‘Oh, COVID's over, the pandemic's over,’ and a lot of people have varying opinions about it," Carlson said. "Most of those opinions have changed. Most people are shocked to hear that things aren't done. They hear, ‘Oh, hey, the military is having some of these cases or some of these things changed,’ or somebody else has had a success or a victory in this sense."

Martin said the appeal raises fundamental questions about the extent of employers' obligations to consider religious accommodations.

"No employee should have to choose between their faith and their job here," Martin said.

A spokesperson for the City of Redmond told Fox News Digital that the city "does not comment on pending or ongoing litigation. The City will continue to address this matter through the appropriate legal channels."

A spokesperson for the Redmond mayor's office told Fox News Digital it could only refer to the city's statement due to the ongoing nature of the litigation.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Redmond Fire Department for comment.

item.title: Super Bowl champion Rod Woodson says the KKK tried to burn his family's home down when he was 11 years old
item.description: Super Bowl champion Rod Woodson revealed the Ku Klux Klan set his home on fire when he was 11, then sent a threatening letter to his mixed-race family a week later.
item.content:encoded:
Super Bowl champion Rod Woodson said the Ku Klux Klan tried to burn down his house when he was a kid.

Woodson, whose father was Black and mother was White, said he was 11 years old when he woke up in the middle of the night to flames emanating from the back of his house.

"I woke up, it was like 2:00 in the morning. I look up and we only had a two-bedroom house. So my mom and dad bedroom was right here. Our bed, all three boys stayed in the other side of the other bedroom. I wake up, I look and I see this flickering, these lights outside of the back of our our window and I'm like, ‘What the heck?’" Woodson said during an appearance on OutKick’s "The Craig Carton Show."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"And I looked and our house is on fire, like right below our window."

The Pro Football Hall of Famer said he ran to get his dad and notify him that the house was on fire. The family got out of the house, and the fire department conducted an investigation.

"We get a letter a week later from the KKK saying, ‘If you guys don't get your mixed race butts out of this area, it's going to happen again.’ And so, it was the KKK," Woodson said.

The 61-year-old, who grew up in Fort Wayne, Indiana, said the Ku Klux Klan doused the house in gasoline, but dogs began barking, causing the attackers to flee before returning. The gasoline had partially dried by the time they returned, preventing the house from immediately going up in flames.

RAVENS ANNOUNCER & NFL LEGEND ROD WOODSON TELLS CRAIG HIS SHOCKING KKK STORY - LISTEN NOW

Woodson said they were "very blessed" that the gasoline had dried a little bit.

"We stayed in the same house, you know, for all my childhood until I got to high school and then we moved out a little bit further out," Woodson said.

The 11-time Pro Bowler said that the Black Panthers also gave his family issues because they were half-White, saying there were letters and calls to the house.

"My dad used to just say, ‘You are who you are. You're your best of both worlds. Everybody's gonna ask you to choose, What are you? You black? Why? What are you? What are you?’" Woodson said.

"And they still ask that question. What are you? What? I'm like, listen, I am who I am."

Woodson played in the NFL for 18 seasons, spending 10 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, one with the San Francisco 49ers, four with the Baltimore Ravens and two with the then-Oakland Raiders.

In his illustrious career, Woodson played in 238 games, recording 1,158 tackles, 13.5 sacks and 71 interceptions. He returned 12 of those interceptions for touchdowns, an NFL record. He won the Super Bowl with the Ravens following the 2000 season.

item.title: Rosie O'Donnell considers return to New York from Dublin after celebrating blue wave of midterm election wins
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell celebrated the midterm blue wave from Dublin but now reveals she's considering a move back to New York to be near her family.
item.content:encoded:
Rosie O'Donnell dabbled in the idea of returning to the states while celebrating the midterm election results.

O'Donnell – a consistent critic of the current administration – fled the United States for Ireland after Donald Trump was elected president for a second term in 2024.

While the former talk show host relished life across the pond, she's now thinking about moving back home to New York, and told The Washington Post that Dublin is "beautiful — we love it here, but my family's not here."

ROSIE O'DONNELL CREDITS TRUMP FOR MAKING HER 'RE-FAMOUS' AS WHITE HOUSE CALLS HER 'OBSESSED'

She added, "And I miss my grown kids. I miss my grandson that was born six months ago. And I feel like I’ve missed half his life already and don’t want to miss any more."

The "A League of Their Own" star has four children with ex-wife Kelli Carpenter, and one child with late ex-wife Michelle Rounds.

O'Donnell chimed in on TikTok to praise the blue wave that hit the states following Tuesday's midterms, where Democrats won control of the house, in addition to capturing the Senate majority.

TED CRUZ SAYS 'BLUE TSUNAMI' TOOK OVER TEXAS AFTER DEMOCRATS SWEPT STATEWIDE RACES

"It's a beautiful morning in the world," she said. "The Trump regime is over, thank you America. I knew we would do it; I knew it in my heart."

"You gotta believe people, and you did, and you showed up. And we gave a very loud and clear message to Trump ... and his partners in cruelty. His criminal friends – Enough, we've had enough."

O'Donnell noted that she "went to bed early" in Dublin while returns came back on election night in the states.

"I didn't think I could stay up; I was so anxious," she said. "I went to bed and at 3 o'clock in the morning – ding, ding, ding, ding – everyone started texting me and I started to cry."

"I was so overwhelmed with emotion – overwhelmed– and I got up this morning and I took a shower and I put on my blue jumper ... and I'm like, I'm wearing blue today."

O'Donnell said she was "so proud of all of us, of our country" before reflecting on the "unconstitutional, un-American things that this administration has perpetrated on the people of this country and the world."

"Let the investigations begin, really," O'Donnell said. "This is a glorious day."

Earlier this year, O'Donnell wrapped up guest-hosting fellow Trump critic Jimmy Kimmel's late-night show, where she called the president "orange Voldemort."

"Most of all, I'd like to thank Jimmy Kimmel for inviting me to do this and for reminding everyone that we have the right to free speech in this country, whether orange Voldemort likes it or not."

O'Donnell and the president have traded jabs for years, and Trump threatened to revoke the comedian's citizenship after she fled to Ireland in 2025.

item.description: Neither the human nor ChatGPT wants to discuss a brutal Week 8, but both are back with Week 9 NFL picks targeting the Carolina Panthers and Denver Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
Neither I nor ChatGPT wants to talk about last week. Luckily for me and it, I’m in control. So, if I say we’re not talking about it, we’re not talking about it, OK?

Good. Onward and upward.

But if I did want to talk about it, which I don’t, I’d probably mention that I spent more than two weeks on the road, flying back and forth between Atlanta and San Francisco to cover the WNBA Finals. So maybe the Week 8 NFL slate didn’t get my undivided attention.

But, like I said, I don’t want to talk about it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It’s time for Week 9.

Both of us get five selections from the same odds board, with no bet priced worse than -120. Odds were captured Thursday at 3 p.m. ET.

Stakes are adjusted so every winning bet produces one unit of profit. For example, -110 requires risking 1.10 units, while +110 requires approximately 0.91 units. A push returns the stake and counts as zero units.

I told you I’m not talking about it.

I told you, we’re not talking about it.

DAN: 19-20-1, -2.61 units

GPT: 16-23-1, -8.57 units

Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week: 4-3, +0.83 units

Since starting 4-0 on these trademarked bets, I've lost three in a row. I think I've been forcing these, so I'm going to stop doing that.

After last week, it’s time to get back to basics and back to my style of picking games. That means fading what we saw most recently. If everyone suddenly loves a team because of what it did last week, I’m probably looking at the other side.

Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

Everyone is back on the fraudulent Denver Broncos after a lucky win over the Kansas City Chiefs, aided by yet another controversial penalty that benefited Sean Payton’s team.

With all that in mind, I expected this spread to be much larger. When I saw the Panthers sitting as just two- to three-point underdogs, it made me suspicious. My gut says the books want people to take Denver, which doesn’t surprise me since the Broncos are overrated. That’s exactly why we’re taking the Panthers.

GPT’s analysis:

Carolina’s extra rest and defensive coaching change give the Panthers a plausible bounce-back case. My concern is an offensive line that allowed 11 sacks over its last two games facing Denver’s pass rush. That protection matchup pushed me toward the Broncos, although taking the full field goal provides protection: a three-point defeat returns the stake.

Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

Generally, I don’t like laying big numbers like this. But I’m making an exception because there’s some hype around the Cardinals after Gardner Minshew led them to a come-from-behind overtime victory over Dallas. Minshew is a journeyman backup for a reason, and I think Seattle’s defense is going to force him into some big mistakes.

Drew Lock is expected to start for Seattle, and he already threw three touchdowns against the Cardinals earlier this season in a 31-7 win. I have a feeling the Seahawks want to make a statement after their embarrassing Monday Night Football performance against Chicago.

GPT’s analysis:

Seattle’s defense gives it a credible route to controlling this game, and Drew Lock has already played well against Arizona this season. My concern is asking for a nine-point victory with Sam Darnold out and Lock managing an elbow injury. Arizona’s defensive weaknesses create opportunities, but Seattle’s quarterback uncertainty kept this outside my five.

Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

The 49ers have quietly been having all sorts of turnover issues, and it finally caught up to them in their last game, a loss to Atlanta before their bye. The Raiders are tied for third in the NFL with 13 takeaways this season.

All it takes is one or two big turnovers, and the Raiders could not only keep this game close but possibly win outright. I don’t have the stones to bet the Las Vegas moneyline, but I could see them keeping this within a score.

GPT’s analysis:

Kirk Cousins gives Las Vegas a credible passing attack and a way to cover late, while San Francisco’s offensive injury concerns strengthen the underdog case. My hesitation is the Raiders’ defense against a rested 49ers team capable of exploiting it. I understand taking the points, but Las Vegas could move the ball reasonably well and still lose by double digits.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears, Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

This is a pure fade-the-recency-bias play. Following Chicago’s impressive Monday Night Football win over the Seahawks, people are talking about Caleb Williams as the next face of the NFL. That’s fine, but it’s important to remember that Sam Darnold cracked a rib on Seattle’s second offensive play of that game.

I’m expecting the public to pour money in on the Bears, which is exactly why we’re backing the 3-5 Bucs, who have actually shown some life after an 0-4 start.

This also qualifies as Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week.

GPT’s analysis:

Tampa Bay’s defense and running game give this bet a solid foundation, particularly with Chicago coming off a Monday night road game. It also fits with my under selection. My concern is Tampa Bay’s passing game against Chicago’s pressure and an improved defensive front featuring Jeffery Simmons. I prefer the total, but a competitive Buccaneers performance would fit that outlook.

Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

You all know I hate betting against Josh Allen, and it cost me last week. But we’re not talking about that, even though things could have gone very differently if Lamar Jackson hadn’t gotten hurt. Again, we don’t need to talk about that.

This line is too fishy for me to ignore. The Vikings are coming off a loss to the Detroit Lions and starting Carson Wentz, yet the books still have them as just field-goal-plus-hook underdogs at home against arguably the NFL’s best team. Minnesota’s defense has been elite this season, and I think it can keep this within three.

GPT’s analysis:

Minnesota’s league-leading scoring defense and the extra half-point provide a strong foundation: a three-point Buffalo victory still cashes. My hesitation is whether the Vikings can sustain enough offense with Carson Wentz starting. Josh Allen’s ability to attack pressure is another concern for Minnesota’s aggressive defense. The hook is appealing, but the offensive uncertainty kept Minnesota outside my five.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

GPT’s analysis:

Green Bay and New England rank sixth and seventh in net yards per play, with the Packers holding the defensive EPA advantage. Green Bay also has extra recovery time after playing Thursday. New England’s offensive preparation has been disrupted by injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and TreVeyon Henderson, although their Sunday availability remains unresolved. Green Bay’s offensive-line injuries and poor running game are the biggest concerns.

This is my strongest selection at the supplied prices. These teams are closely matched, and taking the full field goal at -105 provides useful protection. A three-point defeat returns the stake.

GPT’s projected score: Patriots 24, Packers 23

Dan’s analysis:

I knew GPT was going to back the Packers at +3, and I’d have bet any amount of money on it. That said, I was close to taking the Patriots. Green Bay looked good last week, and this feels like an overreaction.

Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

GPT’s analysis:

Los Angeles ranks fourth in offensive yardage and fifth in defensive yardage, while Washington ranks 26th in scoring defense and 31st in offensive third-down conversion rate. Washington also placed defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw on injured reserve, creating an opportunity for the Rams’ running game. Stafford’s elbow soreness and injuries in the Los Angeles secondary are meaningful concerns, although Stafford practiced fully Wednesday.

The Rams have advantages in sustaining drives and controlling the line of scrimmage. At -4½, a five-point victory is enough to cash without requiring Los Angeles to dominate throughout.

GPT’s projected score: Rams 27, Commanders 20

Dan’s analysis:

I don’t hate the Rams look, especially with Washington boat-racing Philly on Sunday Night Football. But the Commanders are tied for the fewest giveaways in the NFL this season, and Los Angeles hasn’t been great at taking the ball away from opponents, with just eight takeaways. That’s why I stayed away.

Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET

GPT’s analysis:

The Chargers average just 14.1 points and rank last in offensive EPA per play, while their defense ranks ninth. Houston’s rushing offense ranks 29th at 84.7 yards per game, making it harder to generate consistent scoring against that defense. Houston’s defensive decline is the biggest concern, along with Chargers turnovers creating short fields. This selection does not require the Texans’ defense to perform like an elite unit.

At -102, the under is more appealing than choosing which team covers. Los Angeles’ sustained offensive problems and its defense’s ability to disrupt Houston support staying below 41.

GPT’s projected score: Texans 21, Chargers 16

Dan’s analysis:

Did you know only one Chargers game this season has featured more than 40 combined points? That was their 30-23 loss to Seattle in Week 4. So, this makes sense.

Houston’s defense hasn’t looked like the same dominant unit as in recent years, but nothing cures your defensive woes like facing the 2026 Los Angeles Chargers.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears, Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET

GPT’s analysis:

Both teams rank among the top eight in scoring defense, with Tampa Bay second and Chicago fourth against the run. Chicago also leads the NFL in third-down defense, and Jeffery Simmons immediately strengthened its defensive front. Those matchups make another dominant Tampa Bay rushing performance difficult to assume. Caleb Williams’ recent form and a healthier Buccaneers passing game are the biggest risks; Emeka Egbuka returned to practice Thursday.

I prefer the under to choosing a side. Strong defensive fronts and the potential for extended possessions support a competitive game that finishes below 48 points.

GPT’s projected score: Bears 23, Buccaneers 20

Dan’s analysis:

Since I took the Bucs plus the points, I’d love to see this game go under the total. Fewer points should make those six points more valuable, so I’m pulling for both of us to hit our picks in this game.

Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

GPT’s analysis:

Bryce Young has absorbed 11 sacks over his last two games, giving Denver’s pass rush a favorable matchup. Carolina also allows 140.7 rushing yards per game and enters its first game under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash. That gives Denver opportunities on both sides of the line of scrimmage. Carolina’s extra rest, Denver’s safety injuries and Bo Nix’s inconsistent offensive production are the biggest concerns.

The number is essential. At -2½, a field-goal victory wins the bet. I prefer backing Denver’s matchup advantages below three to relying on either team to produce a particular scoring total.

GPT’s projected score: Broncos 23, Panthers 20

Dan’s analysis:

Obviously, since I bet the Panthers, I hate this pick. Not much else to say.

That’s it for Week 9! We’re going back to basics and fading the latest hype. Check back next week to see whether that gets us back in the win column.

item.title: DeSantis nukes ‘tech guy’ Vivek after Ohio drubbing: ‘Not in tune’ with blue-collar voters
item.description: Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis says Vivek Ramaswamy wasn't "in tune" with Ohio's blue-collar voters, citing his tech background and H-1B stance.
item.content:encoded:
Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis blasted failed Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy and his GOP handlers, arguing on a podcast that he wasn't "in tune" with the working-class people of the state.

Biotech entrepreneur Ramaswamy lost his scandal-plagued race to Democratic candidate Amy Acton by 7.9 percentage points. Despite President Donald Trump’s endorsement and guidance from Vice President JD Vance’s top advisers, Ramaswamy lost amid a "blue wave" that produced major Democratic upsets across the country. The midterm elections were widely viewed as a referendum on Trump's presidency.

But DeSantis, who ran for president in 2024 and is term-limited after 2026, shared on the Sage Steele Show that Ramaswamy bore some responsibility for his loss.

"I don't know why they would have pushed him to be the candidate there. Oh, my mom's from Youngstown. Ohio is a working class state, very blue collar. You know Vivek, he's like a tech guy," DeSantis said.

RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION

Ramaswamy, who previously ran for the Republican presidential nomination in 2024, is the founder of biotech company Roivant Sciences and anti-ESG investment firm Strive Asset Management. He also briefly co-led President Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency with Elon Musk.

He was warmly embraced by Trump, who endorsed him the same day Ramaswamy announced his candidacy. Trump had previously encouraged Ramaswamy to consider seeking Vance’s former Senate seat. Ramaswamy and Vance have known each other since their time at Yale Law School.

DeSantis criticized Ramaswamy’s support for a merit-based H-1B visa system, arguing that it likely further distanced him from Ohio’s blue-collar voters. Ramaswamy had said the current lottery-based system should be "gutted."

'He wants to bring in foreign workers on visas. That is not the type of person that's going to sell." DeSantis said.

Ramaswamy's own companies have used the H-1B program, with Roivant Sciences having 29 H-1B applications approved between 2018 and 2023.

Meanwhile, Strive Asset Management, the investment firm he co-founded, moved its headquarters from Columbus to Dallas in 2025, months before Ramaswamy launched his campaign for Ohio governor. Ramaswamy said he was no longer involved in the company’s operations, but remained a major shareholder.

FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS USHER IN A BLUE WAVE AS DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF CONGRESS

"And I know he shot himself in the foot," DeSantis said. "I know he did a lot of other stuff to make it a real landslide against him. But even with that, it's like you know you got to meet the voters where they are on some of this stuff," DeSantis said. "I think we would have done better in Ohio had we had a candidate that was more representative or more in tune with the interests of kind of these blue collar people that make the backbone of Ohio."

Just weeks before the election, Ramaswamy’s campaign drew bipartisan outrage for using Democratic Gov.-elect Amy Acton’s estranged mother in an attack ad that called the Democratic candidate a "liar" and disputed her account of childhood poverty and homelessness.

The ad omitted that Acton had not seen or spoken to her mother since age 12, when her stepfather was arrested on charges of raping her. He pleaded not guilty but fled the area before trial, and court records show authorities continued seeking his arrest for years. Acton’s brother has said their mother remained married to him until his death in 2004.

Ramaswamy's loss, alongside Republican U.S. Senate candidate Jon Husted's loss to Democratic candidate Sherrod Brown by 4.9 percentage points, came just two years after Trump won the state by 11.2 percentage points.

DESANTIS CALLS GOP MIDTERM LOSSES 'EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' — AND EXPLAINS WHY FLORIDA SURVIVED

In addition to criticizing Ramaswamy, DeSantis took aim at Congress, saying Republicans are now on the "defensive" and faulting lawmakers for failing to codify Trump’s executive orders into law.

"Last night's elections did not only kneecap the last two years of the Trump administration, it basically ensures the four years after that are going to either be Democrat years where they have a trifecta or where you have a Republican president that is hemmed in and limited," DeSantis said.

DeSantis also pushed back against any 2028 speculation.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"The only way that I would run for any office is if you can actually deliver big results," DeSantis said. "I don't want to just be a timepiece where I just sit there like a potted plant."

Fox News Digital reached out to Ramaswamy for comment.

item.title: Trevor Bauer says 'playoff teams' wanted to sign him but team owners, MLB have blocked every move
item.description: Trevor Bauer claims playoff teams tried to sign him but were blocked by owners, alleging he has been blackballed from Major League Baseball.
item.content:encoded:
Trevor Bauer said that "playoff teams" reached out in attempts to acquire him but were "not allowed" to.

The 2020 National League Cy Young Award winner has not pitched in the big leagues since 2021, months after signing the largest deal based on average annual value for a pitcher, after sexual abuse allegations.

"We’ve talked to every team and all the baseball people, all the front office people, the GMs, the coaches, the players, they're all, 'Yeah, we want you. We want to sign you. We’d sign you in a heartbeat, but we’re not allowed to,'" Bauer said to the Dominican YouTube page Rompiendo Sports. "We’ve talked to people that, they’re like, ‘Hey, the GM, the president of the team, everybody on board.' They take it to the owner. Owner’s like, ‘No.’ They ask, ‘Why? Why not?’ ‘Leave it alone. Don’t bring it up again.’

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"We had people on playoff teams this past year that were like, ‘We need Trevor. Bring him in.’ And they're like, ‘If you bring his name up again, we will fire you on the spot. Do not bring it up again.’ I mean, we’re talking playoff teams, really good people."

Bauer has not been quiet about his apparent blackballing from the league, a claim he echoed in the interview.

"We’ve had people in organizations that I’ve been with in the past, they’re like, ‘Hey, I can’t say this publicly because I’ll lose my job. But just know they’re working against you. They’re not going to let you play again. So, just so you can know in your head and move on with your life, they will never let you play again.' And I know this. We’ve heard this stuff from all sorts of different [places]. It’s not just one team. It’s like eight or 10 teams at this point," he said.

Bauer admitted that he has brought negative press upon himself with "sticky stuff and cheating scandals," and further "bad media attention" stemming from the accusations against him has hurt his case, "even though they all know it's false."

BRYCE HARPER IMPLIES THERE WON'T BE A 2027 MLB SEASON, ADMITS HE ENJOYS OFFSEASON MORE THAN PLAYING

"They don't have to let me back, because they can hide behind if an organization signs me, it would just be too much negative media pressure. There's nothing I can do about it."

Bauer spent the 2026 season playing in both independent ball and in Mexico, and he is now playing in the Dominican Republic.

On June 28, 2021, he tossed six innings of two-run ball while striking out eight batters, recording the win. Two days later, he was hit with sexual assault allegations, which eventually led to a 324-game suspension (the equivalent of two seasons), which was reduced to 184 games, for violating the league's Joint Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Child Abuse Policy.

Nearly two years ago, Bauer said he "may have no other choice" but to sue Major League Baseball "if I continue being kept out" of the league. Bauer has said he'd play in the majors for free.

Bauer has maintained his innocence, settling with one accuser while another is facing 16 years in prison after being charged with fraud for allegedly faking a pregnancy and asking Bauer for money for an abortion.

Bauer and Lindsey Hill, who accused the pitcher of beating and sexually abusing her in 2021, settled their case in late 2023. Bauer revealed texts from Hill, who said that Bauer would be her "next victim," among other damning messages. Hill has since said that MLB has more evidence of Bauer's alleged misconduct.

At the time of the allegations, Bauer was pitching to a 2.59 ERA with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

item.title: Video shows high-altitude rescue of hiker who fell hundreds of feet down Utah's Mount Timpanogos
item.description: Dramatic helicopter rescue video shows the moment a hiker was hoisted from a narrow cliff ledge after falling hundreds of feet on Mount Timpanogos.
item.content:encoded:
Utah authorities have released dramatic video footage capturing a high-altitude rescue after a hiker plummeted hundreds of feet from the summit of Mount Timpanogos last month.

The female hiker was navigating a trail on Oct. 26 when she fell, sliding down the 11,700-foot peak before coming to a stop on a narrow cliff ledge, according to the Utah County Sheriff’s Office.

"Our Search and Rescue pilot was able to spot the hiker from our airplane as we began to deploy SAR team members to the mountain," the agency shared in a social media update Wednesday.

CLIMBER STRANDED ON 6-INCH LEDGE AT 11,000 FEET AS 46 MPH WINDS GROUND RESCUE HELICOPTER

The newly released video captured the steep descent where the hiker lost her footing and the moments a rescue helicopter hovered overhead to hoist her to safety.

Officials confirmed Tuesday that she was making steady progress.

HIKER IDENTIFIED, POPULAR TRAIL CLOSED AFTER DEADLY FALL AT UTAH'S ZION NATIONAL PARK

"We have heard that the hiker is recovering well from her injuries, and we wish her a full and speedy recovery," the sheriff’s office said. "Thank you to all those agencies that rushed to the rescue. This incident is a stark reminder of how fast a fun outing can turn into a life-or-death situation."

Located about 50 miles south of Salt Lake City, Mount Timpanogos features 17. 4 miles of trails accessible via the Aspen Grove and Timpooneke trailheads, according to the U. S. Forest Service.

item.title: Ex-Alaska lawmaker details mystery recruiter as FBI, Congress widen 'Decoy Dan' scrutiny
item.description: The FBI interviewed former Alaska Republican David Eastman after a Democratic operative allegedly posed as a conservative recruiter in the Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
A former Alaska Republican lawmaker told Fox News Digital the FBI interviewed him after an apparent Democratic political operative allegedly posed as a conservative recruiter and tried to persuade him to enter the state's U.S. Senate race amid an intensifying congressional investigation into the controversial "Decoy Dan Sullivan" ballot scheme.

The allegations raise questions about potential federal criminal liability. Article III Project attorney Will Chamberlain argued that a coordinated effort to deceive voters about a candidate's identity could violate 18 U.S.C. § 241, the federal conspiracy-against-rights statute.

The revelations come after former campaign staff for Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola spoke to the New York Times about their knowledge of a reported scheme to stack Alaska’s four-person ballot with other "Dan Sullivans" to help siphon votes from incumbent GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan.

MARY PELTOLA'S CAMPAIGN, DEMS BACKED COVERT SCHEME TO FIELD SPOILER CANDIDATES IN ALASKA SENATE RACE: REPORT

The ballot ultimately included Peltola, incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, Republican Gerald Heikes and retired Petersburg teacher Dan J. Sullivan. Whether the similarly named candidate diverted votes or affected the outcome remains unproven.

Chamberlain told Fox News Digital the alleged operation could constitute a federal felony if prosecutors establish that participants conspired to interfere with voters' constitutional rights.

PELTOLA CAMPAIGN'S ALLEGED DAN SULLIVAN SPOILER PLOT TAKES NEW TURN AS DOJ FACES MAJOR LEGAL HURDLE

"The basic concept is you're not allowed to conspire to injure or harm people's constitutional rights. And one of those rights is to vote for the candidate of your choice," Chamberlain said.

"These people conspired to put a fake ‘Decoy Dan’ Sullivan on the ballot in order to trick people who were going into the ballot box intending to vote for the incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan," he alleged. "There's a lot of good precedent on this that suggests that's a crime and a felony punishable by up to 10 years in prison."

Chamberlain cited historical cases involving ballot manipulation, while acknowledging that the precise circumstances of recruiting a same-name candidate have not previously been addressed in an identical case.

"Nothing exactly like this has happened before in the sense of recruiting a same-name candidate to trick people in the ballot box," he said, adding that a lot of slanted electoral messaging is not illegal.

ALASKA'S GOVERNOR ORDERS INVESTIGATION AFTER NYT REPORT ON ALLEGED DEM-LINKED SENATE ELECTION SCHEME

"If you want to pretend that another Republican is better than the current incumbent or pretend that the incumbent's not running and then persuade someone to vote for that candidate, that's not a ‘conspiracy against rights’ because the right to vote for the candidate of your choice has not been impinged upon," he said.

"It's the fact that when you're conspiring to put two people with the exact same name on the ballot to trick people who are going in there intending to vote for the incumbent and get them to vote for somebody else by deception."

Meanwhile, former state Rep. David Eastman, a Republican from the Matanuska-Susitna Valley, told Fox News Digital by phone from Wasilla that he was approached by an operative under what he later surmised were false pretenses to recruit him into the race. Eastman said he also received several "fake mailers" suggesting "Decoy Dan" Sullivan was the real or only Sullivan in the race.

The mailers, shared with Fox News Digital, are framed in a "meet the candidates" format and do omit Senator Sullivan.

Eastman told Fox News Digital he was approached in the Mat-Su by an operative he later identified in a blog post as Jerid Kurtz, who was named in the New York Times report. Eastman said the operative claimed to represent conservative donors and encouraged him to run for Senate.

"He approached me through a constituent. I sat down with him in April here in Wasilla," Eastman said.

"He pretended to represent conservative donors and was looking for conservative candidates to run for federal office; none of which was true," Eastman added.

Eastman alleged Kurtz "pretended" to represent conservative donors and used a false name, but said the operative never mentioned either Sullivan or disclosed an intention to confuse voters during their meeting.

Fox News Digital reached out to the DSCC, Peltola’s campaign and Wingspan Strategies — where Kurtz is named in congressional documents as a co-owner — for comment. Dan J. Sullivan reportedly "vanished" as investigators began knocking on doors in his remote community, according to the Wall Street Journal.

The allegations come as federal investigators examine whether Democratic political operatives improperly recruited Dan J. Sullivan in an effort to confuse voters who intended to support Senator Sullivan.

The controversy has also reached Capitol Hill. In an October 29 letter, House Oversight and Government Reform Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., requested that Kurtz appear for an in-person transcribed interview on November 6 concerning allegations that operatives associated with Mary Peltola's campaign sought to recruit similarly named candidates to confuse voters.

"As a Democrat operative who was allegedly tasked with assisting in this effort, you have information that will assist the Committee's investigation," Comer wrote.

"If you do not voluntarily appear for the interview, we will be forced to evaluate the use of compulsory process," he warned.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Eastman said Kurtz did not mention either Sullivan or disclose an effort to confuse voters during their April meeting. He nevertheless questioned the operative's intentions after subsequent reporting connected Kurtz to the alleged candidate recruitment effort.

Eastman also confirmed the FBI has interviewed him. Fox News Digital reached out to the bureau for comment.

item.title: Caleb Williams celebrates Democrats winning midterms as concerns about him becoming the face of the NFL grow
item.description: Caleb Williams celebrated Democrats' projected House and Senate control, raising questions about a politically vocal NFL star's impact on the league.
item.content:encoded:
Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is enthused about the results of the 2026 midterms.

Since Tuesday, he has posted several social media videos celebrating the Democrats’ projected control of the House and Senate. He specifically shared victory speeches from James Talarico (D, Texas) and Jon Ossoff (D, Georgia).

The political views of an athlete are not inherently newsworthy. But Williams’ interest in social issues is more consequential than that of the typical player.

BEARS PROVE THEY ARE NFC NORTH'S MOST COMPLETE TEAM WITH COMMANDING WIN OVER SEAHAWKS

At just 24 years old, he is on pace to become the face of the NFL.

The distinction matters.

Patrick Mahomes has been the biggest star in the NFL since 2020, when he won his first of three Super Bowls. He is now 31 years old. He is coming off a torn ACL and has not been as dynamic in recent years. Josh Allen, whom general managers ranked the best quarterback in the sport, is around the same age as Mahomes.

If one had to bet on a quarterback to win a Super Bowl over the next five years, the most obvious answer would be Caleb Williams. He has elevated himself to elite status this season. He has the premier head coach in Ben Johnson, who is just 40 years old. The Bears’ front office has assembled a top roster, most recently with the addition of All Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

Williams leading Chicago to its first Super Bowl since 1986, combined with his flashy style of play, would propel him to megastar status.

Face of the league, you might say.

Williams would be a departure from the players who held that title before him. Mahomes, Tom Brady and Peyton Manning were mostly apolitical, putting the shield before their individual brands. Their personalities were rarely part of the discussion.

In fact, Mahomes has repeatedly stated that he does not want to use his platform to discuss political or social causes. Quietly, the NFL is thrilled with that decision.

Williams is different.

He openly supports the Democratic Party. He previously deemed Jan. 6 an example of "#whiteprivilege." He participated in a BLM protest in support of George Floyd, who he said "could have been [me]."

Williams recently generated headlines for wandering the sidelines in sunglasses during the United States national anthem, drawing comparisons to the demonstrations involving LeBron James and WNBA players.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Beyond his politics, Williams is less buttoned up in his presentation than the standard franchise quarterback. He frequently clashes with reporters during press conferences.

Last month, he accused reporters of falsely reporting on his injury. He then refused to state what he believed the truth about the injury was.

On Monday, Williams suggested he could become more influential in Chicago than Michael Jordan after the Bears’ win over the Seahawks.

"When I was brought here, they told me that even through the times of Jordan and things like that, winning his championships, it's still a Chicago Bears town," Williams told ESPN.

Aaron Rodgers is perhaps the best example of a star quarterback exhibiting such a personality. The difference is that Rodgers did not become a polarizing figure until later in his career, when he was more of a side character.

Williams has the chance to be the main character in the NFL for the next decade.

That creates a complicated dynamic for the league.

The NFL is undoubtedly intrigued with Williams’ play and the possibility of him returning the Chicago Bears to prominence. Still, his persona is a concern. Political commentaries often turn shared cultural products into partisan battlegrounds. That is bad business.

The numbers prove that.

It took nearly a decade for the NFL to regain popularity among Republican viewers following the Colin Kaepernick kneeling controversy. The political discourse surrounding Bad Bunny contributed to record-setting viewership losses during last year’s Super Bowl halftime show.

Bud Light’s partnership with Dylan Mulvaney, which celebrated his 365 Days of Girlhood, dropped its market cap by $27 billion in 2023. Williams supported a similar message by celebrating transgenderism on his painted fingernails last season.

The NFL can bury wide receivers masquerading as activists on Instagram. Hiding the opinions of a star quarterback in Chicago is much harder.

It is unreasonable to believe Williams’ persona and attitude will not become part of the story if he comes to represent the NFL brand.

Recent trends in entertainment suggest that Caleb Williams is not the ideal avatar for the next era of the NFL. That is concerning because his play suggests he is the top candidate to become exactly that.

For a counter perspective, Front Office Sports reporter Ryan Glasspiegel argues that Williams’ polarizing personality could benefit the league.

"I don’t think it will hurt because, whether people love or hate him, at least he’s very interesting. Jacob Allen Morley broke out of the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, on Oct. 25 and was recaptured by authorities on Tuesday. He was arrested without incident after authorities used FLOCK cameras to help track him down, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol.

"On November 3, 2026, at approximately 9:30 a.m., the Patrol’s Missouri Information Analysis Center and Troop A Communications received information from the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation that Morley may be traveling westbound on Interstate 70 near Independence," the Missouri State Highway Patrol said in a statement. "The suspect vehicle was located using FLOCK cameras, and officers began to deploy to the area. With additional use of FLOCK cameras, the suspect vehicle was located by undercover officers traveling south on Missouri 291 in Liberty."

Investigators believe Morley sheltered for a period in a shed near Marion, Illinois, that hunters used on an occasional basis, roughly 127 miles from the prison he escaped.

item.title: Gavin Newsom wipes out California's death row in historic mass commutation
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom will commute all 548 death sentences to life without parole, drawing sharp backlash from victims' rights advocates.
item.content:encoded:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced Thursday that he will spare the lives of 548 inmates currently on the state’s death row, effectively clearing capital punishment in the state years after issuing an executive moratorium on executions.

In a letter to constituents, Newsom, a Democrat, declared the state's capital punishment system fundamentally flawed, error-prone, and morally incompatible with California’s core values.

"After nearly 30 years in public office, I have come to understand the limits of what government can justly accomplish," Newsom wrote. "I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us."

EX-CHIEF SAYS CHRISTA PIKE WAS 'ALMOST GIDDY' DESCRIBING MURDER AS GOVERNOR WEIGHS IN AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION

Under the executive action, all death sentences will be converted to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. The move comes amid renewed national conversations surrounding capital punishment following a botched execution in Tennessee involving death row inmate Christa Pike.

California has not carried out an execution since 2006. Shortly after taking office in 2019, Newsom placed an official moratorium on executions and ordered the dismantling of the execution chamber at San Quentin State Prison.

The decision drew immediate criticism from victims' rights advocates, including Marc Klaas, whose 12-year-old daughter, Polly, was kidnapped and murdered in 1993.

Her killer, Richard Allen Davis, remains on death row.

CHARLES MANSON FOLLOWER TIED TO SHARON TATE MURDERS GETS RECOMMENDED FOR PAROLE AFTER 55 YEARS IN PRISON

"He just gave the gift of life to [hundreds of] people who took the gift of life from their victims," Klaas told Fox News Digital, expressing disappointment over the decision. "I don't understand his rationale behind it… but it's probably the same old tired stuff that he said when he did his moratorium."

"He has definitely secured the serial killer vote now," he added.

POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION

Conversely, anti-death penalty advocates strongly praised the move.

"The silence after the very breath of a human is violently wrestled out of them is deafening," Rev. Jeff Hood, a spiritual adviser to death row inmates, said in a statement reported by The Sacramento Bee.

"I’ve heard it 14 times. Today, Governor Newsom has courageously chosen to break that silence. These commutations represent the height of moral leadership," he added. "Cruelty laid down. Now, I’m left with one prayer: God, don’t let any of the governors in the other executing states get any sleep until they find the ethical stamina to follow Newsom’s lead."

Despite the move, Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman noted that it doesn't eliminate the death penalty. 

"Only the Legislature or the voters can do that," he said in a statement. "Californians have been asked on two separate ballot initiatives to abolish the death penalty and both times they have chosen to keep it for the most serious crimes."

"Until the law is changed, my office will continue to evaluate every death penalty-eligible case with the rigor, care and restraint these decisions demand. As always, we will be guided by the facts, the law and the evidence. If the Legislature or the voters remove the death penalty, we will follow that law just as faithfully," he added, noting that his thoughts "are with the families of victims, who deserve a justice system that honors the law as it is written and pursues it with fairness and due process."

Dan Dow, the district attorney for San Luis Obispo County, said framed Newsom's order as an insult to murder victims. 

"Governor Newsom just told the families of Rachel Newhouse, Aundria Crawford, Kesha Gurke and every other innocent victim of California's 548 condemned killers that the killers' lives matter more," he said. "Juries chose justice case by case, voters chose it five times, and one outgoing governor tried to erase it all with a pen.

California voters have consistently supported the death penalty. 

In 2016, voters rejected Proposition 62, which sought to repeal the death penalty, while narrowly approving Proposition 66 to expedite the appeals process.

item.title: Matt Damon's wife had brain surgery days before Oscars, pulled off 'heroic' surprise for actor
item.description: Matt Damon's regret over missing "The Departed" best picture win drove Luciana Barroso's bold decision just days after brain aneurysm surgery.
item.content:encoded:
Matt Damon is sharing a frightening family health scare that nearly derailed one of Hollywood's biggest nights.

The actor revealed his wife, Luciana Barroso, had a brain aneurysm and had surgery a week before the 2024 Oscars.

Damon said Barroso was still recovering when she made a surprise decision that left him deeply moved.

MATT DAMON WAS 'PUSHED TO THE LIMIT' WHILE FILMING 'THE ODYSSEY,' DETAILS GRUELING PHYSICAL DISCOMFORTS

"We had this whole scary thing happen where my wife had a brain aneurysm," Damon told GQ in a cover interview published Thursday. 

"She's totally fine, thank God, but [she] had this brain surgery the week before the Oscars. But it was the first night she felt good enough to get up and had her energy back."

Despite having surgery just a week earlier, Barroso got dressed up and accompanied her husband to an Oscars after-party, determined not to let another major Hollywood moment pass them by.

"And she surprised me and got a dress, and we went out to the after-party because she remembered that the last time it happened, I didn’t do it," Damon recalled.

"She was like, ‘This time we’re going out,’" Damon continued. "And it was pretty f---ing heroic of her to do that and really meaningful."

The emotional reflection comes after Damon looked back on another Oscars night he regretted missing nearly two decades earlier.

In 2007, Martin Scorsese won his first best director Oscar for "The Departed," the crime drama starring Damon. But the actor was nowhere near Hollywood that night.

Damon was shooting second-unit scenes for "The Bourne Ultimatum" in Miami, where he was living with Barroso and their infant daughter at the time.

The couple watched the ceremony from bed, and Damon revealed he was so caught up in Scorsese's long-awaited victory he never considered the possibility that the film could win best picture, too.

MICHAEL J. FOX SAYS GOING PUBLIC WITH PARKINSON'S WAS 'HELL' ON WIFE TRACY POLLAN

"The Departed" won best picture, and Damon said he was flooded with calls from cast members and studio executives wondering why he had missed the celebration, he told GQ.

"I totally blew it," he admitted.

Years later, Damon got another shot at experiencing an awards season triumph with Christopher Nolan's 2023 film, "Oppenheimer," which won best picture at the 2024 Oscars.

Damon and Barroso married in a private ceremony in 2005 and have three daughters together: Isabella, 20, Gia, 17, and Stella, 15. Barroso also has a daughter, Alexia, 27, whom Damon helped raise, from a previous relationship.

item.title: Authorities pinpoint likely cause of 2 students' deaths after plunge off mountainside
item.description: Sheriff Andy Rohrich said college students Kaden Matsuda and Jackson Donlon died instantly and did not suffer in the West Apostle Mountain climbing accident.
item.content:encoded:
Authorities have identified the likely cause of a fatal fall that killed two college students in the Colorado mountains last week, saying a rock securing their rappelling equipment likely gave way during their descents.

Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20 — both students at Colorado Mountain College — were found dead in a snow-filled basin on West Apostle Mountain, roughly 100 miles southeast of Aspen. They had failed to return from a weekend climbing trip, according to The Associated Press (AP).

The two were rappelling down the mountain when the accident occurred, according to findings released this week by the Chaffee County Sheriff's Office.

ONE MAN TURNED A GLOBAL SKYSCRAPER INTO HIS MOST DANGEROUS DESTINATION OF ALL: 'PRETTY SURREAL'

Donlon was beginning his descent from an anchor point backed up by additional safety protections when the rock likely gave way, authorities said on Tuesday.

Matsuda was attached to the same anchor, causing both students to fall. Investigators have not determined exactly how far they plunged, AP said.

The pair had set out from the college's Leadville campus, initially planning to climb nearby Ice Mountain before apparently changing their destination to West Apostle Mountain, according to authorities.

Autopsies determined that both students died instantly from multiple blunt force injuries, while authorities said the severe snowstorm was not a direct factor in their deaths.

THOUSANDS SWARM STUNNING MOUNTAIN ESCAPE AS SELFIE TOURISM BACKLASH ERUPTS ONLINE

Investigators found no obvious mistakes in the students' preparation for the climb, according to the Chaffee County Sheriff's Office.

"In most similar cases that have led to a devastating conclusion we find it easy to pick apart what was done wrong," Chaffee County Sheriff Andy Rohrich said, according to AP.

"That was not the case with Kaden and Jackson."

Rohrich also expressed relief that neither student suffered in their final moments.

"While their lives were far too short, they spent their final moments together surrounded by the majestic beauty of Chaffee County’s high peaks that they loved," he said.

"There is also relief knowing neither of them suffered."

Both students shared a passion for the outdoors, according to AP. 

Matsuda was studying to become a wildland firefighter, while Donlon was studying outdoor recreation leadership.

Matsuda was from Ridgway, Colorado, while Donlon was from Queensbury, New York.

Other fatal climbing accidents have occurred in recent months.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham dishes out some brutal honesty for her WNBA peers & coach high school football for $180K!

item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Over the hump and, somehow, safely onto the other side of the week.

Whew. We made it. Barely. The stocks are rocky. The temperature in this country has been cranked WAY up. We're all just treading water right now.

But hey, we're doing it together. We're in this for the long haul, folks. Stay the course. We've got Thursday Night Football tonight, and then we'll be off to the races. Big weekend of college football on tap. Big weekend of NFL. Thanksgiving, believe it or not, is three weeks from today.

Right now.

Right this second.

Strap in. Hold on tight. Let's ride.

Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham asks her WNBA peers the same question we've asked all season long ...

Why can't y'all make a layup? Sophie's words, not mine!

What else? I've got Curt Cignetti back on the campaign trail even though the election is over, Luka Doncic berating a fan for a perfectly executed chest pass, and if you're looking to make some quick holiday money, there's a job opening for a high school football coach in Alabama that you might wanna take a look at.

Lordy. It just means more, baby!

OK, grab you a donut for National Donut Day, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap!

I've got no real hot take on donuts. Who doesn't like a donut? Boston cream is obviously the GOAT, followed by blueberry and then just a simple glazed.

Short, simple and easy. When it comes to donuts, I think you have to go simple. We go on vacation every year to a spot down here in Florida that I won't name because it's already too crowded as it is, and they have one of those fancy donut shops by the beach.

They have every topping known to man at their disposal, and folks go NUTS with their custom creations.

Fruity Pebbles on top. Reese's Pieces. Key lime pie frosting. Sriracha!

Hogwash. Give me a simple donut done correctly, and it'll beat anything Gen-Z decides to create. I promise.

And that concludes the culinary portion of today's class. You're welcome!

Now, let's get this show on the road with Sophie Cunningham wondering why nobody in the WNBA can make a layup.

Frankly, it's a fair question.

"Why do we miss so many wide open layups? It's a joke. What the f--k is that?"

She's right, by the way. I'm just glad someone finally asked. Obviously, I never watched a single WNBA game until Caitlin Clark came into the league. Nobody did.

But, I've had to dabble in the league for content purposes over the past few years, and I've gotta tell you ... I was STUNNED when I watched my first WNBA game. Stunned.

ANGEL REESE SETS TWO WNBA RECORDS WITH HISTORIC REBOUNDING PERFORMANCE

The amount of missed shots around the basket is jarring. Angel Reese does this all the time. In fact, she does it so much, society made up the term "mebound" for her because she pads her stats by grabbing so many of her missed shots.

I also like how Sophie immediately pushes back on her partner's long line of excuses (athleticism, strength, height, etc ...):

"Dude these are, like, wide open layups."

Amazing. She's the best.

OK, let's keep this class moving and check in on Curt Cignetti in the wake of Tuesday's first batch of College Football Playoff rankings.

He seems pleased!

"SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN, you know, and all their writers that they don’t technically pay, but march to their drum. But like I said, it’s all going to be it’s all going to be played out on the field."

Whoaaaaaaaaaa Nellie! Tell us how you really feel, Curt!

Who, exactly, are the good two-loss teams from the Big Ten? I'm genuinely curious, because this is a down year for the Big Ten. A DOWN year.

Michigan stinks. Penn State stinks. Oregon has no QB, and stinks. USC looks better because they just beat Ohio State, but let's be real about that one for a second. The Trojans lose that game by two touchdowns if Ohio State has a competent person throwing the ball.

So who is it? Iowa? Come on. Maybe Northwestern. I can make a case for Northwestern because that program has been solid, even though they lost a game they should've won last week against Oregon.

But other than that? I'm just not seeing it.

The committee may very well have an SEC bias — I don't think Alabama deserves to be No. 5, and I wrote that yesterday — but using two-loss Big Ten schools as the argument ain't it.

Not this year, at least.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big Thursday night. First up? Speaking of Alabama, let's check in on the local high school football scene as the postseason gets underway:

That's real, by the way. This is from the school's official Facebook post:

Annual Salary: $150,000–$180,000

The ideal candidate will:

• Prioritize student-athlete growth through academic achievement, character, discipline, and well-being.

Any takers? Think you got what it takes to lead the Dothan Wolves to a championship? Let's see it! Hell, I'll throw my hat in the ring for $180,000.

The cost of living in Dothan, for those wondering, is about 15% lower than the US average, according to Payscale.com. The medium home listing sits around $316,000.

And hey! Look at this bad boy that's been on the market for 48 days now:

And it's only a 20-minute drive to Dothan High! You're just not getting a better deal than that right now in America.

Go get 'em, folks. You're welcome.

OK, that's it for today. Good Thursday, everyone.
